body:
Found while comparing link-foundation/start's CI/CD with this template (https://github.com/link-foundation/start/issues/234). Checked against template HEAD `0a62b80` (2026-10-10). Each item below caused a false result in start, and each is fixed there in PR https://github.com/link-foundation/start/pull/235. The fixes are linked for reuse.

### 1. `bump_type` has no `default:`, so dispatching through the API gets HTTP 422

`.github/workflows/release.yml:22-29`:

```yaml
      bump_type:
        description: 'Manual release type'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [patch, minor, major]
```

- **Reproduce:** `gh workflow run release.yml -f release_mode=instant`, which gets HTTP 422 because `bump_type` is required and has no default. `CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md` §17 makes the same point: "the dispatch API answers HTTP 422 without it".
- **Fix:** add `default: patch`. A test that every `required: true` input has a `default:` keeps it fixed. See start's `js/test/ci-workflow-invariants.js`, test "gives every required dispatch input a default" (commit https://github.com/link-foundation/start/commit/9f07fed).

### 2. `links.yml` passes `--cache` but never persists `.lycheecache`; the failure message points at an artifact that is never uploaded

- `links.yml:74-75` passes `--cache --max-cache-age 1d`, but nothing restores or saves `.lycheecache`. Every run therefore starts cold, and `--max-cache-age` never applies. The comment at line 46, "Typical run: <1min with lychee cache", describes a cache that never exists.
- `links.yml:137` prints `Report location: lychee/out.md (available as a workflow artifact if configured).` No `upload-artifact` step exists, so a failed run leaves nothing to inspect.
- **Reproduce:** run the workflow twice. The second run's lychee log shows no cache hits, and the run page has no artifacts.
- **Fix:** start's `links.yml` (commit https://github.com/link-foundation/start/commit/a4d3784):

```yaml
      - name: Restore lychee cache
        uses: actions/cache@v5
        with:
          path: .lycheecache
          key: cache-lychee-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: cache-lychee-
      # ...
      - name: Upload lychee report
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code != 0 }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: lychee-report
          path: lychee/
          retention-days: 14
```

  These have regression tests: "persists the lychee cache it asks for" and "uploads the report the failure message points at" in start's `js/test/links-workflow.mjs`.

### 3. `Format changeset with Prettier` swallows its own failure

`release.yml:994`: `npx prettier --write ".changeset/*.md" || true`.

- A Prettier error (a bad glob, a missing binary, a parse error) is hidden. The PR is then opened with an unformatted changeset, and the error only shows up later, as a red format check on that PR.
- **Fix:** drop `|| true`. If an empty glob is the concern, check for files first.

### 4. Related, already fine here: lint warnings and npm propagation

This template already does both of these correctly. Start had copied older versions:

- `eslint --max-warnings 0`. Start's `eslint .` exited 0 on warnings.
- A long post-publish registry wait, with conflict-as-landed handling (`publish-retry.mjs`). Start waited only 60s.

Mentioned only so the other templates can be checked for the same gaps.
title: release.yml bump_type has no default (HTTP 422); links.yml --cache is never persisted and its report artifact is never uploaded; prettier || true hides errors

body:
The JS template's example-app workflow has the same direct generated-push pattern that failed in link-assistant/calculator issue 195.

Reproducible example:
1. A push to main starts a workflow that regenerates preview/screenshot artifacts.
2. While that job is running, another main-writing workflow commits first, such as an automated release/version bump.
3. The preview job commits generated files and runs plain `git push origin HEAD:main`.
4. Git rejects the push with `main -> main (fetch first)` / `failed to push some refs` because the remote branch advanced.

Concrete evidence from calculator:
- https://github.com/link-assistant/calculator/actions/runs/28194099705 failed in Update Screenshots with a non-fast-forward push rejection.
- The failure happened while the release pipeline from the same merge was also writing to main.

Template location:
- `.github/workflows/example-app.yml` commits preview images with `git push origin HEAD:main` and no rebase/retry path.

Suggested fix:
- Put jobs that write generated files to main behind a shared main-writer concurrency group.
- Replace plain pushes with a helper that does `git push origin HEAD:main`, and on rejection runs `git pull --rebase origin main` before retrying.
- Add a small local regression test using a bare Git remote and two clones to prove the helper handles a non-fast-forward race.

Workaround until fixed:
- Manually rerun the failed generated-artifact workflow after the release/version-bump workflow finishes, or rebase the generated commit locally and push it again.
title: Harden generated preview-image pushes against non-fast-forward races

body:
## Summary

The `release.yml` pipeline publishes to npm and waits for the version to be
indexed (`verifyPublished`), but it never **installs the published package from
npm into a clean project and runs it**. There is no install-from-package smoke
test, so a successfully-published-but-broken package (bad `files`, wrong `bin`
path, misconfigured `exports`) still produces a green release.

## Reproducible example

1. Misconfigure packaging (e.g. drop the CLI entry from `files`, or point `bin`
   at a path that is not packaged).
2. Push a release. `changeset publish` succeeds and `npm view <pkg>@<ver>`
   resolves, so the release is green.
3. A consumer runs `npm install <pkg>@<ver>` and `npx <bin>` — and it fails.

## Why indexing checks are not enough

The release pipeline already polls the registry until the new version is
*indexed* (e.g. `Wait for crate/NuGet indexing`, `verifyPublished`). That proves
the version *exists*, not that it is *usable*. A package can index perfectly yet
be broken for consumers when:

- `files` / `package.include` / packaged paths omit a required file
- the `bin` / `[[bin]]` / entry-point path is wrong or not executable
- `main` / `exports` / the published module shape is misconfigured
- a runtime dependency is declared as a dev-dependency (so it is missing on install)

In every one of these cases the release goes green and the release notes
advertise an install command that does not work.

## Suggested fix

Add a **post-publish smoke-test step** that installs the just-published artifact
from the registry into a throwaway project (NOT the repo checkout) and exercises
each advertised entry point (library import, CLI, and HTTP server if any),
with retries to absorb registry-propagation lag. Fail the release loudly if any
entry point is broken.

## Reference implementation

`link-assistant/web-search` (issue
[#6](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-search/issues/6)) implements exactly
this:

- npm: [`js/scripts/smoke-test-package.mjs`](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-search/blob/main/js/scripts/smoke-test-package.mjs)
  — temp project, `npm install <pkg>@<version>` with retries, then verifies
  library import + `--list-providers` CLI + `serve` HTTP `/health`.
- crates.io: an inline `Smoke-test published crate` step in
  [`.github/workflows/rust.yml`](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-search/blob/main/.github/workflows/rust.yml)
  — `cargo install <crate>@<version>`, run the binary, and compile a fresh
  dependent crate against the library.

Happy to open a PR porting the pattern back to this template.
title: Release pipeline lacks an install-from-package smoke test (indexing check is not enough)
